title: Spin-wave softening across the uniform-to-stripe domain transition in iron garnet film
authors: Titiksha Srivastava, Victor Leroy, Nessrine Benaziz, Nathaniel Findling, Ludovic Largeau, Jamal Ben Youssef, Jean-Paul Adam, Thibaut Devolder, Joo-Von Kim
abstract: Spin-wave spectra across transitions between uniform and textured phases can offer deep insight into both symmetry-breaking physics and self-assembled magnonic bands. However, experiments require a material platform that combines low damping, well-defined textures, and spectroscopic access. Here, we study a Bi-doped iron-garnet film with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA), which undergoes a uniform-to-stripe-domain transition as a function of in-plane magnetic field. Real-space imaging by magnetic force microscopy reveals field-reorientable stripe domains aligned with the in-plane field, while reciprocal-space measurements using thermal microfocused Brillouin light scattering ($μ$-BLS) reveal the softening of a low-frequency spin-wave branch near the transition and the appearance of additional modes in the stripe-domain state. Calculated dispersion relations identify finite-$k$ softening in the Damon-Eshbach geometry ($k \perp M$), with the corresponding wavelength matching the stripe periodicity at the transition. In addition, a $μ$-BLS spectral model reproduces the measured mode frequencies and relative intensities at selected fixed fields. Micromagnetic simulations capture the field-driven formation of the stripe state and reproduce the experimental thermal $μ$-BLS spectra. Our findings establish BiYIG with PMA as a model low-damping platform for studying spin-wave freezing, stripe-domain modes, and reconfigurable magnonic band structures.
summary: This paper characterizes the spin-wave dynamics across the uniform-to-stripe domain transition in $	ext{BiYIG}$ films using combined MFM and $\mu$-BLS measurements. By correlating observed low-frequency mode softening with theoretical predictions, the authors establish a robust model for understanding reconfigurable magnonic band structures in these garnet materials.
main_problem: The study investigates spin-wave spectra across the magnetic phase transition from a uniform ferromagnetic state to a stripe-domain structure in an iron garnet film.
main_result: The research successfully correlated the theoretical prediction of finite-$k$ spin-wave softening with the experimentally observed domain periodicity at the transition point, confirming BiYIG as a model platform for studying magnonic band structures.
method: A combination of experimental techniques—Magnetic Force Microscopy (MFM) and thermal microfocused Brillouin light scattering ($\mu$-BLS)—was used alongside micromagnetic simulations to characterize the magnetic excitations.
model_or_system: The physical system is a Bi-doped iron garnet film ($	ext{BiYIG}$) exhibiting perpendicular magnetic anisotropy ($	ext{PMA}$), which forms field-reorientable stripe domains when an in-plane magnetic field is applied.
key_observables: Spin-wave softening frequency, stripe domain periodicity ($P$), and the evolution of multiple spin-wave branches (e.g., PSSW modes) as a function of applied field.
important_parameters: In-plane magnetic field strength ($H_x$), film thickness ($t=120 	ext{ nm}$), and the characteristic wavevector $k$ matching the stripe periodicity.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on modeling spin dynamics using linearized Landau-Lifshitz equations, and interpreting $\mu$-BLS intensity requires accounting for optical phase accumulation effects.
figures_summary: Figures show MFM images confirming field-dependent stripe domain formation (Fig 2), the evolution of spin-wave spectra via $\mu$-BLS across the transition (Fig 3), and calculated dispersion relations matching experimental softening points (Fig 4, Fig 5).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the physical system and methods (MFM/$\mu$-BLS) to observe the domain transition. It then uses theoretical calculations (dispersion relations) and simulations (micromagnetics) to model the observed spin-wave softening, culminating in a comprehensive comparison of theory and experiment.
why_interesting: The work provides a detailed experimental and computational roadmap for mapping out magnon band structures in patterned magnetic materials, which is highly relevant for understanding emergent collective excitations in condensed matter systems.
